inputs.notes: Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md: mature US operating retailer (thin margins, buybacks, no bank/REIT/LIC/holdco features) -> standard owner-FCF DCF, owner_fcf.md only (no adaptations file -- US filer, USD quote, no material NCI, SBC negligible at 0.33% of revenue so house and street are nearly identical). Fresh build, no prior DCF/Drivers/memory entry exists for BBY. FY0 = FY2026 (fiscal year ended ~1 Feb 2026); FY2026 annual balance sheet was not extracted in the DB (NULL), so the latest available balance sheet is Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended ~1 Nov 2025), which shows net cash of $1,086M -- this is a SEASONAL HIGH ahead of the holiday quarter (BBY builds inventory-financing cash into Q3 then draws it down by fiscal year-end); FY2024 and FY2025 fiscal-year-end net cash was only $269M and $424M respectively, so treat the $1,086M anchor as upper-bound/seasonal, not representative of steady-state net cash. Net cash in all periods is well under 1x the FCF base, so interest income is NOT stripped (immaterial, and not separately disclosed as a KPI). Historical revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs (all 3yr and 5yr windows measured from FY2021-23 pandemic-peak endpoints) are negative or deeply depressed because FY2021-22 revenue ($47.3B/$51.8B) was a pandemic demand pull-forward that has since normalized to ~$41-43B -- these CAGRs are NOT used as the growth anchor; the forward path instead anchors to FY2027 guidance (revenue $42.3-42.8B, comps +1.9-3.0%, raised twice in FY2027) and decelerates to a mature-retailer terminal growth of 1.5%. EBITDA margin bottomed at FY2025 (5.12%) and recovered to FY2026 (5.32%); management commentary (Q2 FY2027 beat, raised EPS guide to $6.70-6.90) signals continued margin recovery via Best Buy Marketplace/Ads (high-margin, asset-light) -- base case ramps EBITDA margin to 6.3% by year 10, still well below the FY2022 pandemic-peak 7.55% to stay conservative on the structural competitive/tariff pressure the Analysis JSON flags. Cash tax rate anchored at ~24% (FY2022-26 effective cash rates ranged 16.6-41% on noisy pretax-income proxies; 24% approximates BBY's typical blended federal+state effective rate). SBC and buybacks are both small relative to FCF (SBC 0.33% of revenue, buybacks $273M FY2026 vs $1,258M FCF) -- share count held flat per the flat-count/full-SBC-expense convention; buybacks are value-neutral cash return, not incremental per-share value. 10-year horizon used because margin is still recovering from the FY2025 trough and the marketplace/ads ramp is early-stage (year-5 margin not yet at management's implied longer-run level).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 management guidance (revenue +2.1% at midpoint, comps +1.9-3.0%), NOT the trailing CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All trailing CAGR windows (revenue, EPS, equity, 5yr FCF) are negative because FY2021-22 revenue ($47.3B-$51.8B) was a pandemic-era demand pull-forward that has since normalized to ~$41-43B; using any of these as the forward growth anchor would project a business in structural decline when guidance and recent comps (Q2 FY2027 +4.1%) show renewed low-single-digit growth. The 3yr FCF CAGR (+12.1%) is also not representative -- it is recovering off a depressed FY2023 base after post-pandemic inventory rebuild consumed cash. selected_growth_rate is instead anchored directly to FY2027 guidance and decelerated to a mature-retailer terminal rate; see inputs.notes.

base.narrative: Base case: FY2027 guidance (revenue $42.3-42.8B, comps +1.9-3.0%) plays out largely as raised, and growth decelerates gently to a 1.5% mature-retailer terminal rate as replacement-cycle electronics/appliance demand normalizes. EBITDA margin continues the recovery already visible from the FY2025 trough (5.12%) toward ~6.3% over 10 years as Best Buy Marketplace (asset-light commissions) and Best Buy Ads (high-incremental-margin retail media) scale from their current sub-2%-of-revenue base, partially offset by continued store-fleet rationalization costs and persistent tariff/freight cost pressure on thin hardware margins. Working capital is a modest cash drag on growth (wc_capture -5%) consistent with a physical-inventory retailer where receivables+inventory typically grow faster than payables during a demand upswing. Cash tax rate holds at a normalized ~24% blended federal+state rate. A 12x terminal cap (below the 20x tech-style default) reflects a mature, competitively pressured, low-growth retailer where no buyer pays a growth multiple at exit.

bull.narrative: Bull case: Best Buy Marketplace and Best Buy Ads scale faster and further than guided -- marketplace GMV compounds well past the $1.2B FY2027 run-rate and ads revenue approaches or exceeds $1B with high incremental margin, meaningfully lifting the blended EBITDA margin toward pandemic-peak levels (7.6%) by year 10. An AI-driven PC/device replacement supercycle plus resilient consumer spending sustains comps in the 3-4% range for several years rather than decelerating immediately, and the CEO transition (Bonfig, Nov 2026) executes as smooth continuity rather than a strategic reset. Store fleet optimization improves unit economics faster than the base case assumes.

bear.narrative: Bear case: a renewed tariff shock (the IEEPA ruling leaves the trade-policy path genuinely unresolved, with 30-35% of product sourced from China) or a consumer discretionary pullback drives comps negative for 2-3 years, reversing the FY2027 guidance raise. Margin compresses back toward FY2025-trough levels and stays there as promotional intensity from Amazon/Walmart offsets any marketplace/ads mix benefit, and continued store closures signal share loss rather than optimization. The CEO transition proves disruptive to the marketplace/ads strategic pivot at exactly the wrong moment. Terminal growth of just 1% and a 10x cap reflect a business that has stopped compounding and is defending share in a structurally slow category.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 guidance (raised twice already) plays out, growth decelerates gently to 1.5% terminal, and EBITDA margin continues its post-FY2025-trough recovery toward 6.3% as marketplace/ads scale.
scenario_narratives.bull: Marketplace and Ads scale faster and further, comps stay in the 3-4% range for years, and margin recovers toward the pandemic-peak 7.6% level; CEO transition is smooth continuity.
scenario_narratives.bear: A renewed tariff shock or consumer pullback reverses the guidance raise, margin falls back to the FY2025 trough and stays there, and the CEO transition disrupts the marketplace/ads pivot.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held above the 15% floor (25%) because the tariff/trade-policy path is genuinely unresolved following the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling (unusual regime uncertainty, not a normal cyclical risk) and because BBY's thin ~3-4% operating margin gives very little cushion if promotional intensity or cost inflation returns; this is a real, near-term risk axis rather than a remote tail. Bull weight trimmed to match (25%) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously (marketplace scaling, ads scaling, a smooth CEO transition, AND sustained comp strength) rather than one clean catalyst. Base case at 50% reflects that the FY2027 guidance raise and Q2 beat are real, recent, repeated evidence of a stabilizing/improving business, not merely management's aspiration.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Best Buy is a mature, thin-margin, buyback-and-dividend-funding consumer electronics retailer whose trailing growth metrics are distorted by the FY2021-22 pandemic demand pull-forward. The valuation anchors forward growth to FY2027 management guidance (recently raised twice on real comp-sales strength) rather than the deeply negative trailing CAGRs, and treats the emerging Best Buy Marketplace/Ads businesses as a genuine but still-early margin tailwind layered on a structurally slow, competitively pressured core hardware retail business. A 10-year horizon lets the still-recovering EBITDA margin mature before capitalizing a terminal value, and a 12x base-case terminal cap (below the 20x tech default) reflects that no buyer pays a growth multiple for a mature retailer at exit.
key_risks_to_valuation: Tariff/trade policy remains unresolved after the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling -- a new tariff regime could pressure costs or demand in either direction
Thin ~3-4% operating margin leaves almost no cushion against cost inflation, freight, or renewed price competition from Amazon/Walmart
Marketplace/Ads margin tailwind is early-stage and unproven at scale -- if it stalls, the base case's margin-recovery path does not materialize
CEO transition (Barry to Bonfig, Nov 2026) at the pivotal moment of the marketplace/ads strategic pivot
Structural category headwinds (falling ASPs in TVs/electronics, housing-tied appliance demand) require continually finding new growth vectors just to offset legacy softness

The Q3 FY2026 balance-sheet anchor used here ($1,086M net cash) is seasonally elevated ahead of the holiday quarter; steady-state (fiscal year-end) net cash has historically been $270-425M, so the entry-price/IV net-debt adjustment is modestly generous versus a fiscal-year-end anchor
